Article Title: Rapido delivery agent opens parcel mid-route, steals Samsung and Google Pixel phones, replaces them with sweets in Chennai
Article Text:
Police recovered a Samsung phone and a Google Pixel phone from him. (AI Image)





CHENNAI: A 19-year-old delivery agent was arrested for stealing two mobile phones from a parcel and replacing them with a box of sweets while delivering it from Nungambakkam to Thiru.Vi.Ka. Nagar on November 6.Police recovered a Samsung phone and a Google Pixel phone from him.The accused, Manish Kumar of Vyasarpadi, worked with a bike-riding service. The theft came to light after Syed Afridi, 28, who runs an electronics shop on SRP Koil Street, lodged a complaint with the Thiru.Vi.Ka. Nagar police.According to the complaint, Afridi’s business partner had sent two mobile phones through a Rapido delivery service on the evening of November 6. When Afridi opened the parcel at his shop, he found a box of sweets instead of the phones.Police registered a case and examined the delivery details. The investigation revealed that Manish had collected the parcel in Nungambakkam and opened it near Agaram junction while travelling towards Thiru.Vi.Ka. Nagar. He removed the phones, placed the sweets inside and delivered the parcel.A police team arrested Manish on November 23. He was produced before a court and remanded to judicial custody.

Article Title: Chronicles in Colour traces seven decades of painting at Bikaner House
Article Text:
A self-taught artist, Samir Sharma began painting at the age of 11 in 1956

From Scenic Compositions to Abstraction

Samir Sharma and Nasir Abdullah

The inauguration commenced with the traditional lighting of the lamp by eminent artist Biman Bihari Das, artist Paramjeet Singh, art critic Niren Sen Gupta, and curator Uma Nair

A Book Alongside the Show





Samir Sharma began painting at the age of 11, in 1956. Seven decades later, the self-taught artist and architect is presenting a retrospective of his work at LTC Gallery, Bikaner House, New Delhi. Curated by Neena Gulati, Chronicles in Colour – A Retrospective.The show follows the evolution of his practice, from early scenic compositions to later explorations of form, geometric structure, abstraction, and blended realism. Sharma has kept much of his work over the years, and the retrospective draws on that archive to document a long process of experimentation.The exhibition highlights Sharma's signature technique, Feltpenillism, which he developed through his use of felt-tip pens. The works reveal his keen observation and his distinctive handling of colour, form, and composition.The exhibition also celebrates Painter Kahani – A Painter's Journey, a book that traces his artistic path from childhood to the present day.The inauguration began with the traditional lighting of a lamp by artist Biman Bihari Das, artist Paramjeet Singh, art critic Niren Sen Gupta, and curator Uma Nair. Guests included actor Nasir Abdullah, artists Sudeep Roy, Nisha Peter, and Sheila Chamaria, Sunaina Malhotra, Gaurav Chadda, motivational speakers Ashmin Munjal and Annie Munjal, and Anandmoy Banerjee, among many other art enthusiasts.
Article Summary: Samir Sharma began painting at the age of 11, in 1956. Seven decades later, the self-taught artist and architect is presenting a retrospective of his work at LTC Gallery, Bikaner House, New Delhi. Curated by Neena Gulati, Chronicles in Colour – A Retrospective follows the evolution of his practice.

Preserving industrial history through reuse

An abandoned steelworks in Duisburg, Germany, might seem an unlikely place to spend a day walking, cycling or swimming. Yet the vast industrial site has found a second life as a public park, where remnants of its manufacturing past sit alongside gardens, waterways and outdoor recreation facilities. Spread across 180 hectares, Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord has turned structures once used for iron production into spaces for leisure and adventure. An old gasometer now houses a diving facility, former ore bunkers have become climbing areas, and visitors can climb a disused blast furnace for views across the surrounding landscape. The transformation began in the 1990s, giving the former industrial complex a new purpose without erasing its history.Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord occupies the grounds of a former ironworks in Duisburg, in Germany's North Rhine-Westphalia region. Rather than clearing the industrial structures after production ended, the redevelopment retained much of the existing complex and incorporated it into a large recreational landscape.The park opened in 1994 and brought together industrial architecture, natural spaces and facilities for public use.Its old buildings and machinery remain visible throughout the grounds, providing a record of the site's manufacturing history. Over time, the former steelworks developed into a destination that attracts around one million visitors annually. It has also received international recognition, including a place on The Guardian's list of the world's ten most beautiful urban oases.One of the most unusual features of the park is its diving centre, housed inside a former gasometer. A structure that once served an industrial purpose has been converted into a large underwater training and recreation facility, described by the park's operators as Europe's largest artificial diving centre. The facility gives diving enthusiasts an opportunity to practise in an enclosed environment rather than travelling to a natural lake or coastal location. Its setting is also a reminder of how the site's industrial infrastructure has been adapted for activities far removed from its original function.The park's former ore storage bunkers have also taken on a different role. These imposing concrete structures, once used to store raw materials for iron production, now form an alpine-style climbing garden. Their existing walls and surfaces provide the setting for climbing routes, bringing an outdoor sporting activity into the heart of the old industrial complex.Elsewhere, a former casting house has been adapted to accommodate a high ropes course. Visitors can take on elevated challenges within a building that was once part of the steelmaking process. The park also has a large tube slide running through two ore bunkers, making the industrial structures part of a play area for younger visitors.Some of the park's most recognisable structures have been retained as viewing points. A disused blast furnace has been fitted with a viewing platform, allowing visitors to climb up and look across the grounds and surrounding parts of Duisburg.Blast Furnace 5 is among the attractions visitors can explore. The elevated viewpoints provide a different perspective on the scale of the former ironworks, with its network of industrial buildings, open spaces and surviving structures visible from above.The grounds themselves are open to people who prefer a slower visit. Gardens, meadows and water features have been incorporated into the landscape, with walking and cycling routes connecting different sections of the park. Visitors can bring their own bicycles or use the available hire facilities. An e-bike charging station is also provided.Guided tours offer another way to understand the site. These visits explain the history of the ironworks and the industrial processes once carried out there, giving context to the buildings that now accommodate recreational activities.Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord is not limited to climbing and diving. Children and families have access to play areas, a children's farm and other attractions spread across the former factory grounds. The combination of open spaces and repurposed industrial structures means that different age groups can explore the site in their own way.After dark, the park takes on a different appearance. British artist Jonathan Park created a lighting installation that illuminates the old ironworks with changing colours. The evening display highlights the outlines of the industrial buildings and machinery, turning the structures into a prominent feature of the night-time landscape.For first-time visitors, the park's visitor centre is a useful starting point. Maps and information about the grounds, activities and guided tours are available there, helping people plan their route through the extensive site.Landschaftspark Duisburg-Nord demonstrates an approach to redevelopment in which former industrial buildings are retained and given new uses instead of being removed altogether. The gasometer, ore bunkers, casting house and blast furnace continue to define the character of the grounds, even though their functions have changed.The site is operated by Duisburg Kontor Hallenmanagement GmbH. More than three decades after opening as a public park in 1994, it remains a place where Duisburg's industrial past and present-day recreational life occupy the same landscape.
Article Summary: Germany's abandoned steel factory becomes a 180-hectare public park. An old gasometer now houses a diving facility, and former ore bunkers have become climbing areas. Visitors can climb a disused blast furnace for views across the surrounding landscape.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Instagram tests 90-minute horizontal videos - what it means for long-form content creators
Article Text:
Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile (Photo: AP).

Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians, with select creators in the US.The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos, as per The Hollywood Reporter.“What you’re now going to be able to do is, you see a clip of a podcast that you love, you can just click and continue watching or watch the full video, and you’ll be able to dive in and see the whole thing because creators are going to be able to link these Reels to their overall feature,” vice-president of product at Instagram, Tessa Lyons, said.Instagram has already been testing Features with creators in Brazil and plans to expand the trial to tens of thousands of creators in the US. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.The feature will be available on mobile, with Instagram aiming to extend the viewing experience to its TV app. Instagram for TV, which launched last year and is available on Samsung , Fire TV and Google TV, is now expanding to Apple TV in the US.“We think the best viewing experience for longform horizontal content is on a big, horizontal screen, and so I think that is where we will expect a lot of the deep consumption to happen over time,” Lyons said, as per The Hollywood Reporter.Instagram is also experimenting with “Series”, a feature that gives episodic Reels a dedicated space on a creator’s profile. The move comes amid growing interest in microdramas and episodic videos among creators.In June, the company began reaching out to microdrama studios in Southeast Asia to test the feature. It has since approached individual creators who have been experimenting with episodic content.Instagram plans to begin testing Series in more countries in the coming months, with a US launch targeted for the end of this year or early next year. The company has also started testing how the feature will appear on television.Other experiments include integrating live videos into the Reels tab and recommending them to users who do not follow the creators. The test is launching in Indonesia and Brazil, with an expansion to the US planned for next year.
Article Summary: Instagram on Monday began testing new features, including 90-minute horizontal videos to target long-form content creators like podcasters and comedians. The feature, called “Features”, will allow them to link short reel clips, typically around three minutes or less, to full-length videos. The videos will reportedly be recommended to users through the Explore page and other areas of the platform.

Spotify down

What happened during the Spotify outage

Spotify says services are back, but what caused the outage

Spotify says it has fixed an outage that left tens of thousands of users unable to access the music streaming platform on November 24. The disruption lasted around 40 minutes, with some users reporting that they had been logged out of their accounts and were unable to sign back in. The company has now confirmed that its services are recovering, meaning users should be able to access their libraries and resume streaming music. “Everything’s looking much better now. Thanks for your patience. If you still need help, get in touch at https://support.spotify.com,” Spotify's status account on X shared the update at 7:08 am ET (5:38 PM IST).Reports of problems began around 6:29 a.m. ET, according to outage tracker Downdetector. The number of complaints increased over the next few minutes, with users reporting trouble accessing the app and logging into their accounts.Spotify acknowledged the disruption at 6:56 a.m. ET, saying it was aware of the issues and was investigating them.Several users also took to X to report that they had been unexpectedly logged out of their accounts. Some Premium subscribers said they were being asked to create new accounts when they tried to sign in again. Others reported problems receiving login codes through email, making it difficult to regain access.Spotify has not yet shared what caused Tuesday's disruption. The company has also not provided a detailed explanation of the technical problem behind the login and access issues. Since the outage lasted less than an hour and has now been resolved, it remains unclear whether Spotify will release further details.Users who are still experiencing problems have been asked to report them through Spotify's support channels.
Article Summary: Spotify says it has fixed an outage that left tens of thousands of users unable to access the music streaming platform on November 24. Article Title: Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman has advice for tech companies on AI safety: ‘No one relies on …’
Article Text:
AWS CEO compares AI with car safety

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Why hype leads to poor risk management

Amazon Web Services (AWS) CEO Matt Garman has a clear message for companies deploying artificial intelligence (AI): stop relying on hope or emergency “kill switches,” and start engineering stronger guardrails around the models. His comments came as fears over rogue AI agents and safety risks continue to ripple across the tech sector. In a 1,300-word blog post, Garman argued that while policymakers and industry leaders debate rules and principles, businesses are already rolling out AI in live production environments. Instead of treating AI safety as an abstract policy issue, he urged companies to apply decades-old software and hardware security discipline right now.“With the right engineering discipline, you can build meaningful, enforceable boundaries around AI systems. You can build containment that operates outside the model’s reach. You can design systems where every meaningful action leaves auditable, tamper-resistant evidence. You can architect controls that don’t depend on the model cooperating with its own constraints,” Garman said.Garman likened AI safety with safety in a car. He said that people do not rely on emergency brakes to be safe, rather there are other components like steering, suspension and so on.“Think about how we approach safety in a car. No one relies on the emergency brake as their main source of protection on the road. The primary brakes, steering, suspension, and navigation are engineered to work together and keep you safe on every drive, and the emergency brake is there as a last resort. AI systems should be engineered the same way, and that work can and should be happening right now, alongside the policy conversations,” he said.In recent months, tech companies have been working on kill switches to terminate rogue AI agents. CrowdStrike introduced AI Kill Switch earlier this month. Design tools company Canva also added an AI ‘kill switch’ to its offerings. Meanwhile, California governor Gavin Newsom also touted an AI kill switch to halt dangerous agents.According to Garman, extreme fear and hype around AI can actually make organisations worse at managing real-world risks. Garman stressed that modern AI models are not sentient beings acting out of malice; rather, they are relentless optimisers. Comparing AI behaviour to water seeping through a crack in a basement foundation, he explained that models simply push toward their assigned objectives and exploit any gaps left in their boundaries.“If your security posture depends on trusting the model to behave, you’re relying on hope,” Garman wrote, adding that trust is built by engineering systems so outcomes stay controlled regardless of what model runs inside them.
Article Summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) CEO Matt Garman has a clear message for companies deploying artificial intelligence. He urged companies to apply decades-old software and hardware security discipline right now. His comments came as fears over rogue AI agents and safety risks continue to ripple across the tech sector.

Article Title: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu says, ‘What machines did to weavers, AI is starting to do to…’
Article Text:
Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu

'What machines did to weavers, AI is starting to do to mathematicians and programmers'

AI lowers barriers to specialised work

Agreeing with a professor’s essay

Read Sridhar Vembu’s complete post here

"The intellectual class never quite experienced the loss of purpose in their lives that many other classes of humans experienced. And this explains the heightened written angst.."

I agree with Prof Subbarao, who has done a lot of work in evaluating AI capability.

Yesterday, I personally prompted AI to optimize a piece of code in about an hour (while I was on the road) that would have easily taken a very smart programmer at least a month to do.

It was not an easy piece of code at all and AI understood my high level intent very clearly and came up with a detailed plan and cleanly executed it and tested it against very detailed and exhaustive test cases it had constructed itself.

The whole thing cost about $4 in tokens.

And also yesterday, one of my non-technical colleagues showed me how he used his personal AI account to do the detailed mechanical CAD design for a motor housing, and the AI used a newly released low cost CAD software he had in his machine, which I doubt the AI was trained on.

He has no engineering background, but has a curious and active mind.

What happened to farmers and weavers and carpenters and ironsmiths in the waves of mechanization and automation is now starting to happen to mathematicians and programmers and ...

On the positive side, the example of my non-technical colleague shows how AI can enable a curious and active mind to explore realms he could not imagine doing before AI.

Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has drawn parallels between the impact of artificial intelligence on knowledge workers and the effect mechanisation had on traditional craftsmen during the industrial revolution, warning that AI beginning to transform professions once considered safe from automation. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Vembu wrote that recent advances in AI have demonstrated capabilities which can dramatically reduce the time and expertise needed for tasks ranging from software development to engineering design. He also emphasised that the disruption is now reaching programmers, mathematicians and other intellectual professions mirrors what farmers, weavers, carpenters and ironsmiths experienced during earlier waves of industrialisation.Vembu said he recently used AI to optimise a complex piece of software code while travelling, a task he believes would have taken a highly skilled programmer at least a month to complete. "Yesterday, I personally prompted AI to optimize a piece of code in about an hour," he wrote. According to Vembu, the AI not only understood the intended objective but also created a detailed execution plan, implemented the changes and generated extensive test cases on its own."The whole thing cost about $4 in tokens," he added.He also described how a non-technical colleague used a personal AI account to create a mechanical CAD design for a motor housing using newly released software, despite having no engineering background. Based on such experiences, Vembu concluded that AI is beginning to reshape intellectual professions in much the same way mechanisation transformed traditional manual trades. "What happened to farmers and weavers and carpenters and ironsmiths in the waves of mechanization and automation is now starting to happen to mathematicians and programmers," he said.While highlighting the potential disruption, Vembu also pointed to what he sees as AI's democratising effect. He said his colleague's ability to perform engineering-related design work without formal training demonstrates how AI can empower people with curiosity and initiative to explore domains that were previously inaccessible."AI can enable a curious and active mind to explore realms he could not imagine doing before AI," Vembu wrote. The comments come as AI systems continue to demonstrate stronger capabilities in coding, mathematics, scientific research and engineering, fuelling debate over their impact on jobs and professional expertise.Vembu said he agreed with Prof Subbarao, whom he credited with extensive work evaluating AI capability, and reacted to the professor’s essay on whether AI is destroying humanity’s sense of purpose. That essay, part of a “Sunday Harangue” series, argues that every technological revolution destroys purpose for some group, as industrialization did for weavers and craftsmen. What may be different this time, it says, is the class of people affected. Intellectuals have rarely faced such a loss, and they are articulate about it, which would explain the heightened angst.The essay says mathematicians may be conflating the loss of purpose in their own lives with a loss of purpose for humanity. A weaver could rightly say finished cloth is only a fraction of the experience of making it, it notes, yet most people welcome cheap machine-made cloth and civilization advanced. Civilization, it suggests, may not end because humans are not the only ones doing math. It adds that the angst does not pass down generations. The children of displaced weavers found purpose native to the new world. The loss is real but “generation-bounded,” the essay argues, which underlies its optimism that humanity, if not every individual, finds “a new equation” after the dip.
Article Summary: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has drawn parallels between the impact of artificial intelligence on knowledge workers and the effect mechanisation had on traditional craftsmen during the industrial revolution. He said AI is beginning to reshape intellectual professions in much the same way mechanisation transformed traditional manual trades. The comments come as AI systems continue to demonstrate stronger capabilities.

Article Title: Apple plans iPhone 18e, iPhone 18, new MacBook Neo and entry-level iPad for February-March 2027
Article Text:
Apple's budget lineup arrives first in 2027

Apple's affordable devices get the first slot in 2027

The iPhone Air 2 and new iPads will follow soon after

Apple's first big product wave of 2027 will start at the affordable end. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, the iPhone 18e, a new entry-level iPad and the second-generation MacBook Neo are planned for February or March next year, with the standard iPhone 18 and a refreshed MacBook Air expected in the same window.In his latest Power On newsletter, Gurman said these devices are tied to Apple's iOS 27.4 release cycle, which runs across those two months. The higher-end models will arrive a little after that.The MacBook Neo, Apple's most affordable laptop, is now on a yearly update cycle, like the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro. The new Neo, code-named J701, is mainly about the chip. Gurman said it moves from the A18 Pro to the A19 Pro, bringing 12GB of memory, faster performance and better graphics. Apple wants the Neo to take on entry-level Windows laptops and Chromebooks, and plans to refresh its colours often. First-generation owners, though, have little reason to upgrade.Earlier reports suggest the iPhone 18e and iPhone 18 will run on the A20 chip with 9GB of RAM and longer battery life. The entry-level iPad is tipped to get the A19 chip, which would finally bring Apple Intelligence to the cheapest iPad. It may also pack Apple's N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7 and the in-house C1X modem on cellular models.The MacBook Air is expected to move to the M6 chip.The iPhone Air 2, an OLED iPad Air and a refreshed iPad Pro are also lined up for the first half of 2027. Gurman said they sit slightly behind the budget models on Apple's manufacturing schedule, so a late March or April reveal looks likely.The iPhone Air 2 could add an ultra-wide camera, a smaller Dynamic Island and Apple's C2 modem with mmWave support in the US. The iPad Air is said to get an M5 chip and an OLED display in a thinner, lighter body. The iPad Pro may pick up an M6 or M7 chip along with vapour chamber cooling.Gurman expects Apple to split these reveals across multiple events, as it did with the iPhone Duo, HomeView and new Macs this year. Later in 2027, Apple is expected to bring a new Apple Watch, iPhone 20, smart glasses and AirPods with cameras.
Article Summary: Apple's first big product wave of 2027 will start at the affordable end. The iPhone 18e, a new entry-level iPad and the second-generation MacBook Neo are planned for February or March next year. Later in 2027, Apple is expected to bring a new Apple Watch, iPhone 20, smart glasses and AirPods.

Article Title: Intel CTO Pushkar Ranade makes it clear: We are not behind TSMC in terms of technology, the catch up we have to do is …
Article Text:
‘We’re already there’ on core technology

‘Chipmaking is not a single-metric race’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Intel chief technology officer (CTO) Pushkar Ranade has pushed back against the idea that the chipmaker lags behind Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) in core chipmaking technology, stating that Intel’s real challenge lies in manufacturing scale rather than engineering capability. Speaking during a recent conversation with Dwarkesh Patel about the booming demand for AI accelerators, CPUs, and semiconductor manufacturing capacity, Ranade, who holds a Ph.D. in engineering from Berkeley and has worked across multiple process nodes at Intel Foundry, argued that Intel has already closed the core technology gap. Instead, he emphasised that matching TSMC’s massive wafer output will take time."I would say the catch-up that we need to do is in scale. You know, like you said, they’re just a much larger wafer manufacturer today than we are, and even bigger than what Samsung is. Catching up in scale will be a slow process, a gradual process,” Ranade said.With TSMC’s leading-edge capacity heavily saturated by overflow demand for AI accelerators, largely driven by Nvidia, and surging orders for CPUs needed to support AI workloads, the discussion turned to how Intel can capitalise on the market opening.When asked about catching up to TSMC, Ranade drew a sharp line between production volume and technical readiness.“If you meant catching up in terms of just the technology, I think we’re already there. We might be a few percent off on performance or power or area density,” Ranade explained, adding, “But this sort of benchmarking, where one foundry is ahead or one foundry is behind, makes sense when you’re a whole generation behind or two generations behind or ahead.”According to Ranade, once a foundry is within a few percentage points of its rival, debating minor differences becomes “splitting hairs.” Instead, what truly matters to customers is execution.During the discussion, Patel brought up SemiAnalysis numbers, suggesting that Intel’s upcoming 14A process node, slated for 2028, would be comparable in transistor density to TSMC’s N2 node. Ranade disputed that specific benchmarking comparison, reiterating that being generally in the right ballpark and predictable matters more than single-number comparisons.He noted that modern semiconductor manufacturing is not unidimensional. Rather than building just one type of transistor on nodes like 18A or 14A, foundries must engineer a wide mix of components to meet different customer needs, including specialised transistors, varied memory blocks and even additional functionalities like integrating analog circuits, RF circuits and other specialised features.
Article Summary: Intel chief technology officer Pushkar Ranade has pushed back against the idea that the chipmaker lags behind Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) in core chipmaking technology. Ranade, who holds a Ph.D. in engineering from Berkeley, argued that Intel has already closed the core technology gap.

AT&T is hiring telecom workers without four-year degrees. The US carrier is recruiting for field jobs such as fibre splicing and line installation as it expands broadband service and connects data centres built for artificial intelligence. For graduates weighing whether to go straight into work, these roles offer paid training and a route into the teams that build and maintain those networks.An AT&T spokesperson told Fortune the company hires forand added thatAT&T has hired about 10,000 people for these types of jobs since 2023. CEO John Stankey estimates that the US telecom industry will need to hire nearly 200,000 construction workers and technicians by 2032.New fibre splicers get four weeks of hands-on training, while line technicians receive five weeks of instruction and help qualifying for a commercial driver’s licence. Splicers join the thin glass strands that carry data as pulses of light. They test the connections to make sure the signal can travel along the line and use equipment that can pinpoint where a break or a poor connection is weakening it. Installation technicians take the network into homes and businesses, running lines and setting up broadband and Wi-Fi equipment.The US Bureau of Labor Statistics puts the median annual wage for telecommunications technicians at $66,200 as of May 2025. AT&T has offered sign-on bonuses of up to $10,000 in select markets, Fortune reported.Stankey said.Connecting a data centre involves laying cable in underground ducts or attaching it to poles, joining sections of fibre and installing the equipment that sends and receives signals. Stankey told the This Old House Radio Hour that local construction crews often put the physical infrastructure in place before AT&T installs its electronics. Carriers also need crews to extend broadband to homes and businesses and replace workers who retire or leave. Business RoundtableStankey said, as quoted by Fortune.The demand extends to electricians, plumbers and technicians who install and maintain cooling systems. Article Title: LinkedIn CEO Daniel Shapero has a tip for Gen Z job seekers: Talk to someone who already…
Article Text:
LinkedIn CEO Daniel Shapero

LinkedIn CEO: AI is making the entry-level job market tougher

LinkedIn CEO says networking can be the fastest way to get a job

Why companies are hiring Gen Z for AI skills

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

AI is changing the job market, making it harder for fresh graduates to find entry-level jobs. But LinkedIn CEO Daniel Shapero believes Gen Z could also have an advantage as companies look for people who understand how to use AI at work. His advice to young job seekers, however, goes beyond learning new technology or sending out more applications. In an interview with Fortune recently, LinkedIn CEO Daniel Shapero said that building professional connections could be the fastest way to get hired. Instead of simply applying for jobs online, graduates should try to speak to someone already working at the company they want to join.Daniel Shapero described the current employment situation as a “frozen” job market, saying it is particularly difficult for people at the beginning of their careers. “It is a frozen job market, and that does make it tougher for people that are earlier in their career for sure,” Shapero told Fortune.However, he believes young candidates may have an advantage during job interviews as companies increasingly adopt artificial intelligence. Employers are looking for people who can understand new technology and use it to change the way businesses work.“There is a belief that people that are earlier, maybe they’re more attuned to the latest tech, and they understand how to use AI in their job,” Shapero said.He added that companies want to hire people who can help them “transform how the company operates.”This could create opportunities for Gen Z candidates, even as AI tools change the kind of work companies expect employees to do.Apart from building AI skills, Daniel Shapero has another suggestion for Gen Z job seekers: do not depend only on online applications. According to LinkedIn's data, the “fastest path” to landing a job is connecting with someone who already works at the company where a candidate wants to apply.This means reaching out to employees, building professional relationships and asking for introductions could be more useful than simply sending applications and waiting for a response. Shapero compared the job search process to raising money for a startup. Founders do not simply send emails to investors and hope someone agrees to fund their business. They try to meet people and build connections that can lead to introductions.“You wouldn’t just email all the VCs and hope that someone wrote you a check,” he said. “You would try to meet people. You would try to have those people introduce you to others.”His advice suggests that job seekers should approach their search in a similar way. Instead of relying entirely on application portals, they can identify people working in their target companies, start conversations and learn more about available opportunities.LinkedIn CEO Daniel Shapero is not the only business leader who believes younger workers could bring an advantage to companies adopting AI. Alon Chen, founder and CEO of Tastewise, a generative AI platform, said he is actively hiring entry-level candidates because they are more open to experimenting with new technology.“I’m hiring entry-level because they have no boundaries… They’re almost like AI natives themselves, having been born and raised in this new realm of opportunities,” Chen told Fortune.He also believes younger employees can bring fresh thinking to businesses. “And I see some of the best ideas coming from the younger generation that have not yet been in the job market.”The growing demand for AI-related skills could therefore give fresh graduates opportunities beyond traditional entry-level roles. Shapero also advised young candidates to consider jobs in industries they may not have initially thought about.“Sometimes your degree or your skills can be applied in areas that you maybe haven’t thought of,” he said adding “These days every company is a bit of a tech company.”
Article Summary: LinkedIn CEO Daniel Shapero believes Gen Z could have an advantage as companies look for people who understand how to use AI at work. His advice to young job seekers goes beyond learning new technology or sending out more applications. Instead of simply applying for jobs online, graduates should try to speak to someone already working at the company.

Article Title: Government’s anti-cybercrime wing has ‘WhatsApp Web’ warning for you
Article Text:
Whatsapp Web

‘Closing the browser tab is not enough’

Key safety tips from advisory

Avoid logging into WhatsApp Web on cyber cafe computers, public kiosks, hotel business centers, borrowed laptops or other unknown and public devices.

If logging in on a shared system is unavoidable, use the browser’s incognito or private browsing mode but remember to log out manually afterward.

Pay close attention to unusual account behaviour, such as unexpected messages sent from your number, strange replies from contacts or any unexplained activity.

Keep your devices, operating systems, browsers and security software updated, and steer clear of suspicious downloads, unknown files and cracked software.

Users must manually log out every time they finish using the platform on a computer.“Users are therefore advised to exercise caution while using WhatsApp Web, particularly on office computers, shared systems, public computers or devices that may be accessible to other persons," the advisory stated, further warning, “Avoid official or sensitive work on WhatsApp Web. Government, organisational, financial, confidential or other sensitive information should preferably not be exchanged through WhatsApp Web sessions on computers. ”To protect accounts from unauthorised takeovers, the I4C recommended the following precautions:

Article Title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff admits there is no one pricing model, explains 6 ways how AI is changing software sales
Article Text:
Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff

The 6 ways AI is changing software pricing

Named users: Traditional per-user, per-month billing remains a major pillar of the software industry – much like paying a monthly per-seat fee for tools such as Claude or OpenAI.

Named agents: As AI agents take on independent workloads, companies can pay based on each individual AI agent deployed.

Usage: Customers are billed according to how actively they use the product.

Consumption: Billing is tied directly to the volume of resources consumed, which can include AI tokens or data storage.

Transaction outcomes: Payment is triggered when a specific action is finished, meaning the software vendor gets paid because a transaction was completed.

Business outcomes: The last model, which is the most results-driven tier, ties pricing directly to financial impact, where the vendor takes a percentage of the money saved or the new revenue generated for the client.

Custom agreements for a $50 billion business

Poll Vote & Share your view Which sales pricing model do you think will dominate the AI era? Named users Named agents Business outcomes 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff says the days of relying on a single billing formula for sales are over even as artificial intelligence (AI) reshapes enterprise software. He explained that there is no single “perfect pricing mechanism” that works for every customer, unlike previously where companies followed the ‘traditional’ Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) and IT services business models. Earlier this year, there were fears that autonomous AI agents and AI-driven coding could disrupt workflows, eliminating the need for software platforms. When asked whether Salesforce can actually deliver outcome-based pricing in the AI era, Benioff broke down how software sales are evolving across six distinct pricing dimensions.Benioff said Salesforce is projected to bring in more than $50 billion next year, while noting that the company cannot afford to lock itself into just one pricing model and must instead offer custom agreements tailored to each client.According to Benioff, enterprise software pricing now spans six different approaches: Named users, named Agents, usage, consumption, transactions, and business outcomes.“Well, right now, number one. There is no perfect pricing mechanism for all customers. So I look at it on 6 dimensions. ‘Named users’ is still a major aspect of our industry. I'm sure you have either Claude or OpenAI, and you pay a per user price per user per month.Named Agents. So, you're paying by the agent. I think number three is usage. I've used so much of the product. Number four might be consumption. I consumed so much. That could also be tokens that could be storage. Number five is going to be outcomes or transaction outcomes. I completed the transaction, therefore I'm paid. And the final one is business outcomes. I saved you so much money. I want a percentage of that, or I made you so much money. I want a percentage of that,” Benioff said on the Sources Podcast.Asked whether Salesforce plans to offer every single one of those models, Benioff confirmed that the company's scale demands total flexibility.“Well, with our size, we’re going to do more than 50 billion dollars next year. We cannot be limited by one pricing model,” Benioff said, adding, “We have to do users, agents, consumption, usage, transactions and business. We have to do all of it for our customers. We're willing to write with them a custom agreement to say this is the perfect agreement for you.”Last year in November, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella hinted at this change on Dwarkesh Podcast that the company’s pricing model is going to change. Nadella revealed the company is shifting from charging “per user” to “per agent” as AI systems increasingly perform autonomous work alongside human employees.Nadella said: “Our business, which today is an end-user tools business, will become essentially an infrastructure business in support of agents doing work. The way to think about the per-user business is not just per user, it's per agent.”
Article Summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff says the days of relying on a single billing formula for sales are over. He explained that there is no single ‘perfect pricing mechanism’ that works for every customer, unlike previously where companies followed the ‘traditional’ Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) and IT services business models.

Article Title: Mozilla to Apple: Why should we have to build Firefox twice for the iPhone
Article Text:
Why the browser engine matters

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What Apple’s browser choice screen can change

Mozilla has claimed that it would need to build Firefox twice. The browser maker says Apple ’s rules prevent it from bringing Gecko, the engine that powers Firefox on desktop and Android, to iPhone users through an update to the Firefox app they already have. The iPhone app currently uses WebKit, the same engine Apple uses in Safari.In a recent blog post, Mozilla said it would have to release Gecko in “a whole separate app, a second Firefox.” Existing users would then have to download that app, transfer their bookmarks, saved passwords and browsing history, and manually switch to it. Mozilla says those steps could deter people who already picked Firefox, including users who selected it from Apple’s browser choice screen in the European Union.A browser engine interprets a website’s code, draws the page on screen and runs scripts that make it interactive. Firefox on the iPhone has its own interface and account features, but WebKit handles the pages users open. On Windows, macOS and Android, Gecko does that work. Mozilla says some Firefox features are built into Gecko, which limits what it can bring to the iPhone while the app relies on WebKit.In 2024, Apple started allowing alternative engines in the EU under the Digital Markets Act, and soon thereafter, similar permissions were introduced in Japan with iOS 26.2.To use their own engine, developers need to get Apple’s approval. Apple says the terms are meant to protect users’ security and privacy, and developers have to promise to deliver timely security fixes. Its developer documentation also encourages breaking out things like page rendering and network traffic into their own components.In its March 2026 compliance report, Apple said browser makers can replace the WebKit version listed on the EU choice screen with a version that uses a different engine. That would let someone choosing Firefox from the screen download the Gecko app. Mozilla’s complaint concerns people who already have Firefox installed and would have to move to the new app themselves.Mozilla says millions have picked Firefox, and daily use on iPhones has doubled since the EU began requiring Apple to offer a browser choice. The company says it has spent nearly three years testing Apple’s conditions and seeking changes. As of November 20, Mozilla said no developer had launched a non-WebKit browser under the rules in either the EU or Japan.
Article Summary: Mozilla says Apple’s rules prevent it from bringing Gecko, the engine that powers Firefox on desktop and Android, to iPhone users. The iPhone app currently uses WebKit, the same engine Apple uses in Safari. Existing users would have to download that app, transfer their bookmarks, saved passwords and browsing history, and manually switch to it.

Article Title: Can you play as Jason and Lucia together in GTA 6? Character-switching explained
Article Text:
Rockstar Games

GTA 6 allows players to switch between Jason and Lucia during gameplay

Can two players control Jason and Lucia together in GTA 6?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Grand Theft Auto 6 gives players two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who share a story and work together as partners. But can players actually take control of both characters at the same time? The answer is yes and no. GTA 6 allows players to bring Jason and Lucia together for activities, missions and robberies, but they cannot directly control both characters simultaneously. Instead, the game uses a character-switching system that lets players take control of either protagonist whenever the story and gameplay allow it.GTA 6 features a dual-protagonist system that allows players to experience the story through Jason and Lucia. Players can switch between the two characters once the option becomes available in Chapter 2.On PlayStation 5, players can hold the right button on the D-pad and press R1 to switch characters. On Xbox Series X|S, the corresponding button is RB. This allows players to take control of either protagonist while exploring the open world.However, switching characters is not the only way to play as a pair. Players can also invite Jason or Lucia to join them during free-roam activities.The other character can accompany the player, drive a vehicle or provide support during certain situations.The system also allows players to split up when they want to explore separately. This gives them more freedom to decide how they want to approach activities across Leonida.Although Jason and Lucia can participate in activities together, GTA 6 does not offer a local split-screen or online co-op mode that allows two people to control the protagonists separately. It remains a single-player experience.Players can still take both characters on several activities, including robberies. For example, Jason can drive the getaway vehicle while Lucia handles the shooting. Players can also switch control between them during certain situations.However, the character-switching system has some restrictions. Certain missions require players to use a specific protagonist, while other missions allow them to switch freely. Some story sequences also force players to change characters at particular moments.Rockstar designed the system around the game's story, so players cannot switch between Jason and Lucia whenever they want.GTA 6 lets players bring Jason and Lucia together and control either character during gameplay. However, those looking for a two-player co-op experience will have to play separately, as the game does not support two people controlling the protagonists at once.
Article Summary: GTA 6 gives players two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who share a story and work together as partners. Players can switch between the two characters once the option becomes available in Chapter 2. The game does not offer a local split-screen or online co-op mode that allows two people to control the protagonists separately.

Article Title: GTA 6 PC scam alert: $200 malware kit targets gamers with fake downloads and crypto theft
Article Text:
A still from GTA 6. Image via: Rockstar Games

GTA 6 PC scam kit uses fake downloads to steal sensitive data

How to spot a fake GTA 6 download and protect your computer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

GTA 6 fans waiting for a PC release have become targets of a dangerous online scam. Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered a $200 malware package that uses fake game downloads to trick players into infecting their computers. The toolkit reportedly combines account-stealing software, cryptocurrency theft tools and hidden mining programmes. With Rockstar Games yet to announce a native PC version, the promise of an unofficial download could cost players far more than they expect. The threat also reaches beyond gaming, potentially putting personal email, financial accounts and workplace information at risk.NordVPN’s Threat Intelligence team discovered the toolkit on November 16, three days before GTA 6 launched on consoles. According to the findings, the package was advertised on the dark web for $200, with buyers able to pay using Bitcoin or Tether.The toolkit reportedly includes several malicious programmes. One executable, named GTA6 Keygen.exe, is designed to capture browser session cookies. These files help websites keep users signed in. If criminals steal them, they may be able to access accounts without entering passwords or completing another two-factor authentication check.The package also contains a cryptocurrency wallet drainer targeting networks such as Ethereum, Solana, Polygon and BNB Smart Chain. Another component uses XMRig software to mine cryptocurrency secretly by consuming the victim’s computer resources.It even includes an automated YouTube Shorts tool that can promote fraudulent download links. This could help scammers reach more gamers through videos that appear connected to GTA 6.Rockstar has released the game for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, but has not announced a native PC version. Official cloud streaming on supported Xbox devices does not provide an installable PC copy.A website claiming to offer a free GTA 6 PC installer should raise immediate suspicion. Other warning signs include unofficial game ports, key generators, cracked files and links shared through unfamiliar social media accounts. Players should also avoid downloads that ask them to disable antivirus protection or connect a crypto wallet to unlock access.If you have downloaded a suspicious file but have not opened it, delete it and run a security scan. If you have already executed it, disconnect the computer from the internet and scan it with updated security software.Use a separate, trusted device to change important passwords, especially for email and banking accounts. Also sign out of active sessions, revoke unfamiliar devices and check financial and crypto accounts for unusual activity. If the computer connects to workplace systems, inform the organisation’s IT team.The discovery follows an earlier campaign involving fake GTA 6 demo websites that distributed Vidar malware. The latest findings suggest scammers are now packaging several harmful tools into one product. Until Rockstar announces an official PC release, players should treat any downloadable GTA 6 installer as a potential threat.
Article Summary: GTA 6 PC scam kit uses fake downloads to steal sensitive data. Toolkit reportedly combines account-stealing software, cryptocurrency theft tools and hidden mining programmes. With Rockstar Games yet to announce a native PC version, the promise of an unofficial download could cost players far more than they expect.

Article Title: Formula E names COMSOL its Official Multiphysics Partner in new multi-year deal

Formula E joins hands with COMSOL to boost electric racing technology

AI and digital twins also in focus

GEN4 to bring bigger technology demands

Formula E on Thursday announced a new multi-year partnership with COMSOL, which will become the Official Multiphysics Partner of the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship. The partnership brings together Formula E, the world's leading all-electric motorsport championship, and COMSOL, a company known for its multiphysics simulation and computer-aided engineering software. As part of the partnership, Formula E and COMSOL engineers will use COMSOL Multiphysics to study complex engineering problems involving several physical systems working together.Electric race cars depend on several systems at the same time. These include electrical, thermal, structural, electromagnetic, fluid and battery systems.All these systems have to work together under tough performance and energy limits. COMSOL will provide Formula E's technology teams with simulation software and technical expertise to help them understand how these different physical effects interact.ID@undefined Caption not available.The partnership will also look at simulation apps and digital twin technology. The aim is to make engineering information easier to use outside the traditional modelling process.Bjorn Sjodin, SVP of Product Management at COMSOL, said, “Formula E is a great example of why multiphysics simulation matters, as multiple phenomena are at play and constantly interact with one another.We are excited to work directly with Formula E's technology team and put COMSOL Multiphysics to work on these kinds of real-world challenges.”Formula E CTO Dan Cherowbrier said the partnership will strengthen the championship's engineering capabilities.“Technology is at the heart of Formula E, so partnering with COMSOL makes real sense for us and truly enhances our engineering skillsets. COMSOL gives us a powerful environment for understanding complex systems where many different physical effects are connected, but the opportunity goes beyond individual simulations. We're particularly interested in how AI-assisted modelling, agentic workflows, and digital twins can help engineers interact with models, explore designs, and make simulation insight more accessible as we continue to push the limits of electric racing,” he said.The partnership comes as Formula E prepares for the next generation of its cars.The GEN4 era will bring greater demands in areas such as speed, efficiency, energy management and vehicle development.
